record.context_brief: Covering radius of first-order Reed-Muller codes
record.original_question: Determine the covering radius of the first-order Reed-Muller code R(1, m) when m is odd.

evidence.quote: Open Question 12.6. Find the covering radius of the first order Reed-Muller code R(1, m) for m odd [57]. The problem for even m is solved by the existence of bent functions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer $m$, the first-order Reed–Muller code $R(1,m)$ is the binary linear code of length $2^m$ whose codewords are the truth tables (evaluations on $\mathbb{F}_2^m$) of all affine Boolean functions $f(x_1,\dots,x_m)=a_0+a_1x_1+\cdots+a_mx_m$ with $a_0,a_1,\dots,a_m\in\mathbb{F}_2$. The covering radius of a binary code $C\subseteq\mathbb{F}_2^n$ is
$$\rho(C)=\max_{v\in\mathbb{F}_2^n}\min_{c\in C} d_H(v,c),$$
where $d_H$ denotes Hamming distance. Equivalently, $\rho(R(1,m))$ is the maximum, over all Boolean functions $f:\mathbb{F}_2^m\to\mathbb{F}_2$, of the Hamming distance from $f$ to the set of affine functions (the nonlinearity of $f$).

For even $m$, it is known that $\rho(R(1,m))=2^{m-1}-2^{m/2-1}$, the value being attained by bent functions.

Determine the exact value of $\rho(R(1,m))$ for all odd $m\ge 1$.
artifact.status_search_result: The exact value of the covering radius of $R(1,m)$ for odd $m$ (equivalently, the maximum nonlinearity of Boolean functions on an odd number of variables) is a long-standing open problem. Only small cases are settled; for general odd $m$ only bounds are known, with the classical lower bound $2^{m-1}-2^{(m-1)/2}$ and improved upper bounds such as $\rho(1,2k+1)\le 2\lfloor 2^{2k-1}-2^{2k-3/2}\rfloor$. The problem remains open as of recent surveys.

status_evidence.title: On the norm and covering radius of the first-order Reed-Muller codes
status_evidence.snippet: Improved upper bound rho(1,2k+1) <= 2 floor(2^{2k-1} - 2^{2k-3/2}) for odd m.
status_evidence.claim: Only bounds, not exact values, are known for the covering radius of R(1,m) with odd m.

status_evidence.title: Covering Radius — Survey and Recent Results
status_evidence.snippet: For odd m the situation is much more complicated; the exact covering radius is not known in general.
status_evidence.claim: Survey lists the determination of rho(R(1,m)) for odd m as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: A350271 - OEIS
status_evidence.snippet: For odd n, 2^{n-1}-2^{(n-1)/2} <= a(n) <= 2*floor(2^{n-2}-2^{n/2-2}); exact values known only for small n.
status_evidence.claim: Exact covering radius of R(1,m) is known only for small odd m.
